title: What churchgoers say their church thinks of counseling and medication
subtitle: U.S. Protestant and nondenominational churchgoers attending at least monthly, 2017
caption: Few churchgoers say their church discourages counseling (2%) or medication (6%). But counseling is encouraged far more often than medication, and on medication most say their church takes neither side or are not sure.
note: Churchgoers were asked, "Where does your church stand on the use of psychological counseling or therapy in treating someone with mental illness?" and "Where does your church stand on the use of prescription drugs to treat mental illness?" Encourages combines "strongly" and "a little"; so does Discourages. Neither means "neither encourages nor discourages", which Lifeway's release calls no opinion.

sources.study: Suicide and the Church Research Study (Suicide Remains a Taboo Topic at Churches)
sources.field_dates: Pastors by phone, Aug. 30 to Sept. 18, 2017; churchgoers online, Sept. 15 to 19, 2017
sources.sample: 1,000 Protestant senior pastors (plus or minus 3.2 points) and 1,000 Protestant and nondenominational churchgoers attending at least monthly (plus or minus 3.4 points)
